chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity carries ten (rewards), and a loan carries eighteen, and maintaining ties with (religious) brethren carries twenty, and maintaining family ties carries twenty-four.'

key_terms.الصدقة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity or alms given to those in need
key_terms.القرض: Qard — an interest-free loan; lending with no expectation of profit
key_terms.صلة الإخوان: Silat al-ikhwan — maintaining good relations with one's religious brethren
key_terms.صلة الرحم: Silat al-rahim — maintaining family ties; one of the most emphasized social duties in Islam

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the rewards for charity, loans, and maintaining family ties?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet (SAWW), establishes a hierarchy of spiritual rewards for different acts of generosity and solidarity. Remarkably, a loan (qard) is valued higher than outright charity (sadaqa) because it preserves the dignity of the recipient, while maintaining family bonds (silat al-rahim) carries the highest reward of all. This teaching was addressed to an early Muslim community navigating the social obligations of Islamic brotherhood and kinship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The charity is with ten (Rewards), and the loan is with eighteen, and maintaining good relations with the brethren is with twenty, and maintaining good relationships with the relatives is with twenty four’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated the following Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah has, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said, ‘The reward for giving charity is tenfold, for giving a loan is eighteen-fold, for one for maintaining good relations with friends is twenty-fold, and for one maintaining good relations with relatives is twenty-four-fold. ’ ”
